children: shares fell nearly 5.4% at 10:40 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, as crypto-linked names extended losses. Yahoo Finance's live coverage showed Robinhood down 5.6% before the open, with Coinbase, Circle and Strategy down 7% to 8% after bitcoin fell as low as $64,000, its weakest level since July.

Crypto was already the weak spot. Robinhood's third-quarter results show crypto transaction revenue of $120 million, down 55% from a year earlier, while total net revenue still rose 12% to a record $1.42 billion. Net income fell 14% to $476 million. Funded customers grew 7% to 28.7 million, and total platform assets rose 19% to $396 billion.

Crypto now makes up less than a tenth of total revenue, so the business can absorb the rout better than Coinbase can. The risk is sentiment: weaker crypto prices tend to cool retail trading activity across assets. GuruFocus gives Robinhood a GF Score of 82/100, supported by solid profitability and growth. Shares trade about 14% below the $87.28 GF Value, a modestly undervalued reading, though a model discount does not offset a sharp drop in customer trading. The next marker is Robinhood's November operating data in mid-December, which will show whether equity and options volumes held up while crypto faded.

title: Robinhood Stocks Fall 5.4% as Crypto Rout Pressures a Shrinking Revenue Line
